title: MoRE shared expert pool with depth views
hypothesis: Layer-specific Mirror coordinates recover useful behavior across a reused expert pool with lower actual bytes than independent experts and outperform ordinary MoRE depth embeddings at heldout layer-expert roles.
physical_object: shared expert matrix basis reused across four layers and four expert IDs
mirror_coordinate: factorized depth and expert coordinates for shared basis coefficients
logical_multiplicity: 16 layer-expert operators from one shared matrix basis
controls: MoRE additive depth plus expert embedding

development.selection_metric: heldout operator nRMSE; complete serialized bytes; matrix and code-generation MAC proxy

fresh.reason: single mechanism screen; stop attribution testing after exact native factorization alias

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: Heldout operator nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer actual bytes than independent roles, and strict byte/quality/compute improvement over MoRE additive depth conditioning and native factorization controls.
failure_gate: FAIL for Mirror-specific value if native factorization exactly aliases Mirror, heldout quality fails, or storage/compute gates are missed.
boundaries: Synthetic linear expert operators only; no trained MoRE model, language modeling, router learning, or GPU runtime claim.
Oracle-generated low-rank shared-basis teacher; heldout pairs are role compositions, not independent task checkpoints.
Native bilinear shared-basis factorization is a mandatory exact-form control.
